issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'nên hãy có ân điển' (should have grace) misinterprets the Greek 'εχωμεν χαριν' (we have grace). The Greek indicates that the grace is something the believers already possess/have, not a command to obtain it.
The Vietnamese adds 'Vậy' (So/Therefore) at the beginning, which is not present in the Greek text provided.

The Vietnamese 'hầu việc' (serve/worship) is rendered as an imperative/exhortation ('hãy'), whereas the Greek 'λατρευωμεν' is a present active subjunctive, expressing a purpose or result of having received the kingdom and grace.
